extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing submissions to PVLDB Volume 20 (VLDB 2027) research track
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation-related requirements for submitting research-track papers to PVLDB Volume 20 (VLDB 2027), covering formatting, scope, reproducibility, conflicts, submission caps, deadlines, and related publication policies. Intended to guide authors through what is required for a valid submission and what reviewers/meta-reviewers will consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yearly and monthly submission caps
rubrics_metrics.description: A monthly submission cap of two papers per author and a yearly cap of twelve papers per author (for PVLDB volume 20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cap enforcement: For any paper with ID = k, if one of its authors already has two other submissions with ID < k in the same month, then the paper will be desk rejected. Revision submissions are not counted toward this limit. Cap-based filtering is applied before other checks (e.g., conflict of interest, scope, formatting). Intentional violations of these caps will result in more severe penalties than mere rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA&B artifacts and reproducibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark (EA&B) papers are required to make available all experimental data and related software and submit their experiments for reproducibility evaluation by the PVLDB Reproducibility Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PVLDB volume 20, the initial submission must include a link to the full reproducibility package of all experiments, data, and artifacts with meaningful instructions on how to run the experiments. EA&B papers have no acceptable excuses for not providing these artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory abstract submission for monthly deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory abstract submission by the 25th of the previous month for a paper submission on the 1st of a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is introduced to improve assignment of meta reviewers and reviewers and to indicate out-of-scope papers. Deadlines are strict; no extensions will be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limits by paper category
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be formatted according to the conference camera-ready format. Four categories with page limits (excluding references): Regular Research and EA&B up to 12 pages; Scalable Data Science up to 8 pages; Vision up to 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content, including any appendices and acknowledgements but excluding the references, must fit on the given number of pages. Only the reference section can extend beyond the page limit. See Formatting Guidelines for details. For EA&B, Vision, and Scalable Data Science papers, append the category tag as a suffix to the title in both the paper file and the CMT submission title; the suffix will not be part of camera-ready copy if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind authorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: VLDB is single-blind: authors MUST include their names and affiliations on the first page of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include author names/affiliations contradicts the single-blind policy and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission schedule and strict deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling monthly submission deadlines occur on the 1st of each month, 5:00 PM Pacific Time, with CMT open for submissions from the 20th of the previous month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial reviews usually available by the 15th of the next month. These deadlines are strict; no extensions. Note special windows for revisions (see revision policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision policy and windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial reviews may request a revision; only one revision is permitted. Authors may take up to 2.5 months to produce a revised submission and may submit it via CMT to the appropriate revision track by the 1st of each month for the next 3 months after the revision notification (0.5, 1.5, or 2.5 months after notification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The last three revision deadlines will be May 1, June 1, and July 1, 2027. June 1 is the final revision deadline for consideration to present at VLDB 2027; submissions after this will roll over to VLDB 2028. Final reviews of revisions will usually be available by the 15th of the next month following the revision submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope is assessed solely on the content of the submitted manuscript using three aspects: Core Data Management Focus, Connection to the Database Research Literature, and Evaluation in Data Management Contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core Data Management Focus: whether the paper addresses data management challenges (e.g., scalability, efficiency, storage, lifecycle, queryability) and presents contributions that advance these challenges. Connection to DB literature: whether the paper builds upon or engages with relevant prior work in a non-superficial manner. Evaluation: experimental evaluation should be grounded in motivating data management applications and demonstrate advancement. Scope is not determined by keywords or topic labels; authors outside traditional topics should complete the Self-Assessment of Relevance (SAR) and explicitly highlight key DM challenges and principled contributions, referencing specific sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest declaration responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each author must register themselves in CMT and declare their individual domain and PC conflicts at time of submission; all authors listed in the PDF must register and declare conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the full responsibility of all authors to identify and declare all CoIs with members of the Editorial Board prior to the submission deadline. Conflicts will also be checked with an automated CoI detection tool. Submissions with undeclared conflicts or spurious conflicts will be desk-rejected. Definitions of CoI include: worked at the same university/company in past 5 years or will in next 6 months (accepted job offer); collaborator within past 5 years (joint publication/project/co-organizing); PhD thesis advisor/advisee irrespective of time; relative or close personal friend.

rubrics_metrics.name: No change to author list after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: After a paper is accepted, the set of authors cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the author list is final before acceptance; changes after acceptance are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-nomination requirement by submitting authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission must nominate at least one of its own authors who is a qualified reviewer (authors with at least two previous papers in SIGMOD, VLDB, ICDE, EDBT, or CIDR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no qualified reviewer is available, nominate the best-qualified author. EiCs may draw nominated authors to join the review board as a Light Load Reviewer (at most 1 paper/month, up to 3 papers per submitted paper). If the nominated author does not review an assigned paper, the yearly submission caps of all co-authors are decreased by one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental material availability and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must submit supplemental material (code, data, implementation artifacts) used to produce the paper's results; reviewers and meta reviewers will have access and consider it in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental material should be placed in a publicly accessible archival repository (e.g., public GitHub). Personal web pages are not acceptable. Provide a URL during submission. URLs that raise doubt about security/anonymity may delay evaluation or jeopardize acceptance. If not submitting materials, authors must explain why; compelling reasons (copyright, commercialization, or non-applicability for vision papers) are acceptable. Excuses like 'ran out of time' are not acceptable and must be addressed before acceptance. Meta reviewers will use a standard rubric to assess availability, openness, permanence, and readability of instructions. Accepted papers that meet availability requirements will be awarded an official ACM badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission embargo after rejection/withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not allowed to resubmit work that was previously rejected from the research tracks of PVLDB within one year of the original submission date. A paper withdrawn by the authors after a revision decision will be considered as rejected and the 12-month resubmission embargo applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resubmission embargo does not apply for papers submitted to different tracks (e.g., Industrial and Demonstrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and prior publication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper submitted to PVLDB must present original work not described in any prior publication that is more than 4 double-column VLDB-style pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior publication is a paper accepted for presentation at a refereed conference/workshop with proceedings or an article accepted in a refereed journal. If a PVLDB submission has overlap with a prior publication, the submission must cite the prior publication along with all other relevant published work, even if that prior publication is at or below the 4-page threshold. A paper submitted to PVLDB cannot be under review for any other publishing forum while being considered for PVLDB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-declaration of related concurrent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must self-declare all related submissions that are concurrently under review by the same authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such works must be explicitly cited, marked as 'under submission' in the references list, and reported during submission so the Review Board can assess incremental contribution assuming the earlier submission will be accepted. Failure to disclose related concurrent submissions, if discovered during review, will be treated as a policy breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap-filter ordering and desk rejection practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap-based filtering is applied before other checks; a paper failing the cap rule will be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the paper passes the cap filter, it may be desk rejected for other reasons (conflict, scope, formatting). Revision submissions are not counted toward the caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental material permanence and acceptable repository guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental materials should be placed in a publicly accessible archival repository with well-understood privacy policies and permanence guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard openly accessible file sharing services (e.g., public GitHub). Personal web pages are not acceptable. URLs that raise doubts about security and anonymity of access will cause delays or jeopardize acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failures and intentional violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions with undeclared conflicts, spurious conflicts, or intentional violations of submission caps will be desk-rejected and may face more severe penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: undeclared CoIs discovered during review cause desk rejection; intentional cap violations result in penalties beyond rejection.
